Topics · Who was Muhammad?

Could Muhammad read?

What the Quran says exactly, and what it does not. The word ummi is debated; the argument needs only the text.

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَمَا كُنتَ تَتْلُوا۟ مِن قَبْلِهِۦ مِن كِتَـٰبٍ وَلَا تَخُطُّهُۥ بِيَمِينِكَ ۖ إِذًا لَّٱرْتَابَ ٱلْمُبْطِلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And you did not recite before it any scripture, nor did you inscribe one with your right hand. Then [i.e., otherwise] the falsifiers would have had [cause for] doubt.

Quran · Al-Ankabut 29:48

Read the claim exactly. The verse does not say he never knew a letter. It says two things, both limited to the time before the Quran: he did not recite from a book, and he did not write one with his right hand. Then it says why this matters: otherwise those seeking to dismiss him would have had grounds to doubt. The argument rests on what the Quran says and his neighbours could check: the Prophet was no man of books. That claim is narrow, and so it is strong.

A question for you

What exactly does the verse say, as you read it?

If you sayHe never knew how to read.
ThenThat goes further than the text, which is limited to the time before the Quran and speaks of reciting and writing a book.
If you sayHe was no man of books before it.
ThenThat is closer to the text, and it is all the argument needs.
If you sayI am not sure how to read it.
ThenCommentators ask the same. The next part sets before you the word the debate turns on.

Part 2 of 3

﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلرَّسُولَ ٱلنَّبِىَّ ٱلْأُمِّىَّ ٱلَّذِى يَجِدُونَهُۥ مَكْتُوبًا عِندَهُمْ فِى ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ وَٱلْإِنجِيلِ يَأْمُرُهُم بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَىٰهُمْ عَنِ ٱلْمُنكَرِ وَيُحِلُّ لَهُمُ ٱلطَّيِّبَـٰتِ وَيُحَرِّمُ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْخَبَـٰٓئِثَ وَيَضَعُ عَنْهُمْ إِصْرَهُمْ وَٱلْأَغْلَـٰلَ ٱلَّتِى كَانَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ ۚ فَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ بِهِۦ وَعَزَّرُوهُ وَنَصَرُوهُ وَٱتَّبَعُوا۟ ٱلنُّورَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أُنزِلَ مَعَهُۥٓ ۙ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet, whom they find written [i.e., described] in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins upon them what is right and prohibits them from what is wrong and makes lawful for them what is good and forbids them from what is evil and relieves them of their burden[410] and the shackles which were upon them.[411] So they who have believed in him, honored him, supported him and followed the light which was sent down with him - it is those who will be the successful.

Translator's notes

[410] Difficulties in religious practice. [411] i.e., extreme measures previously required for repentance, and retribution without recourse to compensation.

Quran · Al-A'raf 7:157

﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِى بَعَثَ فِى ٱلْأُمِّيِّـۧنَ رَسُولًا مِّنْهُمْ يَتْلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦ وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَإِن كَانُوا۟ مِن قَبْلُ لَفِى ضَلَـٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾

Translation of the meaning

It is He who has sent among the unlettered [Arabs] a Messenger from themselves reciting to them His verses and purifying them and teaching them the Book [i.e., the Qur’ān] and wisdom [i.e., the sunnah] - although they were before in clear error -

Quran · Al-Jumu'ah 62:2

Translation

Blessed is the man whom you discipline, Yah, and teach out of your law,

Original · Hebrew

אַשְׁרֵ֤י ׀ הַגֶּ֣בֶר אֲשֶׁר־תְּיַסְּרֶ֣נּוּ יָּ֑הּ וּֽמִתּוֹרָתְךָ֥ תְלַמְּדֶֽנּוּ׃

the Psalms · 94:12

World English Bible

The Quran calls the Prophet ummi. The classical commentators mostly took it to mean one who neither reads nor writes. Many scholars today take it to mean one from a people given no scripture. The second verse uses the word for a whole community. So the word is debated, and the argument is not built on it. Notice that the question stands on both meanings. Whether he came from a people with no scripture or did not read, where did the contents of the books come from?

A question for you

Which meaning seems closer to you, and what does it change?

If you sayOne who neither reads nor writes.
ThenThen the question of the source tightens: how did the contents of books reach him without reading?
If you sayFrom a people with no scripture.
ThenThen the question turns: how much of these stories did his people hold?
If you sayThe meaning does not matter much to me.
ThenThe argument does not depend on it much either. It rests on 29:48.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَقَالُوٓا۟ أَسَـٰطِيرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ ٱكْتَتَبَهَا فَهِىَ تُمْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And they say, "Legends of the former peoples which he has written down, and they are dictated to him morning and afternoon."

Quran · Al-Furqan 25:5

There is an unexpected witness: his opponents' own words. Old tales he has had written down, they say, and they are dictated to him morning and evening. Notice the last verb: dictated. They picture texts being read to him, and no scholar poring over them. This may be only their picture, and the verb before it can mean he wrote them or had them written. Still, an opponent's picture deserves a careful reading, because they knew him and were eager to convict him.

A question for you

If it turned out he could read a little, what would change in the argument?

If you sayThe whole argument falls.
ThenThe argument does not stop at knowing letters. The verse speaks of reciting a book, so the question is where that book was and who carried it.
If you sayNot very much.
ThenThen you see that the question is wider than reading: the breadth and depth of what he brought.
If you sayCopying becomes possible.
ThenPossible in principle. The route still has to be found, and that has its own Step.

Your reflection

What is the deepest thing you ever learned without a book, and where did it come from?
